This petition coming on for order this day, the court   the following:
 ORDER 1.

This petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India has been filed by the petitioner, who is posted as Sarpanch of Gram Panchayat, Ahir Bardiya, District Agar Malwa against the impugned order of suspension dated 20.2.2024, passed by the respondent no.3 Sub Divisional Officer (Revenue) Agar Badod, District Agar; whereby, on account of a case registered against the petitioner by the Lokayukt, District Ujjain in connection with offence under section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (hereinafter to be referred to as 'Act of 1988'); the petitioner's services has been suspended.
2. Allegation against the petitioner is that he was caught red handed accepting Rs.20,000/-.

3. Counsel for the petitioner has drawn attention of this Court to section 39(1) (a) of the Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Raj Avam Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam, 1993 (hereinafter to be referred to as "Adhiniyam 1993") which provides that the prescribed authority may suspend from office, any office-bearer against whom charges have been framed in any criminal proceedings, and it is submitted that mere lodging of an FIR is not ground to suspend unless the charges have been framed.
4.

entities.text: Madhya Pradesh Panchayat Raj Avam Gram Swaraj Adhiniyam, 1993
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
In support of his submission that the petitioner cannot be suspended, learned counsel for the petitioner has relied upon various decisions rendered by the coordinate bench of this Court in Vinod Vs. Panchayat and Social Justice, (W.P.No. 18696/2018 order dated 14.1.2019), Farooq Khan Vs.
State of M.P. (W.P.No.9541/2023 order dated 20.7.2023) and in the case of Hukiya Bai (Smt.) Vs.

2 State of M.P and others reported as 2007 (II) MPWN 86 and in these identical cases wherein the Sarpanch, who were the petitioners were suspended on account of FIR having been registered against them in criminal cases, their order of suspension have been quashed.
5. Counsel for the respondent/State on the other hand has opposed the prayer. However, it is not denied that as per Section 39(1)(a) of the Adhiniyam, 1993 the office bearer of Panchayat can be suspended only after the charge sheet has been filed.
6. Heard.

entities.text: State of M.P and others reported as 2007 (II) MPWN 86
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
On due consideration, and on perusal of the documents filed on record, it found that so far as section 39(1)(a) of Adhiniyam, 1993 is concerned the same reads as under:-
39. Suspension of office-bearer of Panchayat.

-
(1) The prescribed authority may suspend from office any office- bearer,-
(a) against whom charges have been framed in any criminal proceedings under [Chapters V-A, VI, IX], IX-A, X, XII, Sections 302, 303, 304-B, 305, 306, 312 to 318,
366-A, 366-B, 373 to 377 of Chapter XVI, Sections 395 to 398, 408, 409, 458 lo 460 of Chapter XVII and Chapter XVIII of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (XLV of 1860) or under any Law for the time being in force for the prevention of adulteration of food stuff and drugs, [suppression of immoral traffic in women and children, Protection of Civil Rights and Prevention of Corruption]; or [(b) x x x.] (2) ......................
(3) ..................
(4).......................
(emphasius supplied)
7.

It is also found that in the case of Hukiya Bai (supra), Vinod (supra) and Farooq Khan (supra)
referred to by the counsel for the petitioner, the coordinate Bench of this Court has already quashed the order of suspension referring to section 39(1)(a) of Adhiniyam, 1993 which is reproduced above,
and in such circumstances, this Court has no option but to allow the present petition and quash the impugned of suspension dated 20.2.2024 on account of applicability of Section 39(1)(a) of Adhiniyam, 1993.

8. It is rather surprising that such a regressive enactment has been made by the State Government to allow the corrupt persons to continue in services even immediately after commission of such serious offence which does not speak well for the intentions of an ideal State.
9. Be that as it may, the petition stands allowed, and the impugned order dated 20.2.2024, is hereby set aside.

10. Let a copy of this order be sent to the Chief Secretary of the State for doing the needful.
